patterns.topic: Security Group rule direction (inbound vs outbound)
patterns.description: Hesitation when deciding which SG gets inbound vs outbound, and whether to reference the peer SG as source or destination. Two-tier patterns (app -> DB) are the typical trigger.
patterns.notes: Mental model that worked: outbound = traffic LEAVING the SG owner; inbound = traffic ENTERING the SG owner. Reference the peer SG, not CIDR. Got the answer right but second-guessed.

patterns.topic: Stateful Security Groups vs stateless NACLs (ephemeral ports)
patterns.description: Distractors that mention ephemeral port ranges in SG questions. Risk of opening unnecessary ranges because of confusion with NACL behavior.
patterns.notes: Rule of thumb: SG = stateful, return traffic auto-allowed, never need ephemeral. NACL = stateless, must open ephemeral on the return side. If 'ephemeral' appears in a SG question, it is almost always a distractor.

trickyQuestions.summary: Two-tier EC2 + RDS MySQL: configure SG rules with least privilege. Pick the two correct rules.
trickyQuestions.myAnswer: Inbound 3306 on DB SG (src=EC2 SG) + Outbound 3306 on EC2 SG (dst=DB SG)
trickyQuestions.correctAnswer: Inbound 3306 on DB SG (src=EC2 SG) + Outbound 3306 on EC2 SG (dst=DB SG)
trickyQuestions.keyInsight: SGs are stateful — never open ephemeral port ranges. Reference SG-to-SG, not CIDRs, for two-tier traffic.
